basis.governing_question: Why did prepaid churn rise in 2025 at Lusitania Telecom, and how can it be brought down?

phases.name: Diagnostic
phases.objective_one_line: Establish why prepaid churn rose in 2025 and agree which retention initiatives Lusitania Telecom rolls out.

gate.label: Initiatives go/no-go
gate.decision: Which churn drivers and retention initiatives go forward into the rollout?

phases.name: Implementation
phases.objective_one_line: Support Lusitania Telecom's rollout of the agreed retention program and track prepaid churn against the baseline.

gate.label: Final readout
gate.decision: Does the steering group accept the rollout and its results to date?

workstreams.name: Customer analytics
workstreams.answers: Which customer groups, behaviors and events explain the rise in prepaid churn in 2025?
activities: Build the prepaid churn baseline from operational data
Test churn drivers by customer segment and period
Interview customers who left prepaid in 2025

workstreams.name: Store operations
workstreams.answers: How do store processes and staff practice affect prepaid customers' decisions to stay or leave?
activities: Interview store staff who serve prepaid customers
Review store operating data and documented procedures
Identify store moments that affect retention

workstreams.name: Retention offers
workstreams.answers: Which retention offers could address the churn drivers found, and which are worth taking into the rollout?
activities: Review documents and data on retention offers in use
Match candidate offers to the churn drivers found
Prepare initiative options for the go/no-go decision

workstreams.name: Retention offers
workstreams.answers: How are the agreed retention offers set up, launched and adjusted for prepaid customers?
activities: Set up the agreed offers and readiness checks
Launch the offers once the workshop confirms readiness
Adjust the offers using results and feedback from stores

workstreams.name: Customer analytics
workstreams.answers: How does prepaid churn move against the baseline as the retention offers go live?
activities: Build the churn tracker against the Diagnostic baseline
Compare churn of customers with and without the offers
Report churn results for the workshop and final readout

workstreams.name: Store operations
workstreams.answers: How do store teams apply the retention offers with prepaid customers, and what stops them doing so?
activities: Adapt store procedures to the agreed retention offers
Train and coach store staff before and during the rollout
Track store adherence through operational data and visits

deliverables.name: Prepaid churn driver findings by customer segment
Store moments that affect prepaid retention
Retention offers matched to churn drivers
Retention initiative options for the go/no-go decision
Launch and adjustment record for the retention offers
Prepaid churn tracker against the baseline
Churn results against the baseline for the final readout
Updated store procedures for the retention offers
Store staff training materials and attendance record
Store adherence report on the retention offers

events.label: Kick-off
events.purpose: Align on scope, team and calendar
events.decision: Does the steering group confirm the scope, team and calendar?
agenda: Align on the problem statement and what the diagnostic must answer
Review the phases, workstreams and the 13-week calendar
Confirm team roles and the steering meeting dates

events.label: Check-in: first findings
events.purpose: Share baseline and churn driver findings
events.decision: Does the steering group confirm the churn baseline as the reference for results?
agenda: Review churn driver findings by customer segment
Confirm the baseline as the reference for tracking results

events.label: Initiatives go/no-go
events.purpose: Decide what goes forward into the rollout
events.decision: Which churn drivers and retention initiatives go forward into the rollout?
agenda: Review driver findings and store moments behind the options
Present the retention offers and the initiative options
Decide which drivers and initiatives go forward into the rollout

events.label: Workshop: launch readiness
events.purpose: Check readiness before offers go live
events.decision: Do the readiness check results support launching the retention offers in stores?
agenda: Present the launch readiness check results
Review the offer specification, store procedures and churn tracker
Decide whether the retention offers go live in stores

events.label: Final readout
events.purpose: Review rollout and results to date
events.decision: Does the steering group accept the rollout and its results to date?
agenda: Present the launch and adjustment record for the retention offers
Review store training, adherence and churn results against the baseline
Decide whether to accept the rollout and its results to date

architect_notes: No Design phase: the archetype's Diagnostic gate selects the initiatives; add Design if Lusitania wants to approve the retention program before rollout.
No Measurement phase: no success criteria are stated and all 13 weeks are planned; confirm the criteria and whether tracking runs past week 13.
Split of the stated 13 weeks into 5 and 8 follows the archetype's typical lengths and three workstreams; confirm the split before quoting.
